Header: Bemisia tabaci , Trialeurodes vaporariorum and Aleyrodes proletella

Prevention: Whiteflies are small white insects found feeding on the sap on the plants on the undersides of the leaves.
Clear weeds in advance of planting crop to reduce overwintering pest stages.
Ensure healthy and vigorous crop growth to reduce whitefly impact with recommended irrigation and fertilization.
Avoid excessive nitrogen levels in the soil, this will be taken up by the crop and favour whitefly survival.
Avoid broad spectrum insecticides to conserve natural enemies such as parasitic wasps, ladybirds, lacewings and hoverflies.
Plant parasitic wasp-attractive plants such as parsley.
Plant whitefly repellant crops such as marigold around the boundary of the field.
Monitoring: Monitor the fields every week during plant growth and observe entire plants for infestation found primarily on stems and the underside of leaves.
Adults are small flies with white bodies and wings found on the underside of leaves.
When disturbed the insects form a small cloud/swarm.
Nymphs are flat, yellowish-white, scale-like and sedentary.
Whiteflies excrete honeydew which can become covered in sooty mould, causing yellowing of leaves.
Use 2 yellow sticky traps/acre to monitor adults populations and for identification.
Plants can tolerate a few whiteflies however if numbers start to establish, take action measures, especially in warm, dry conditions.
Direct Control: Actively remove weeds and other host plants from fields and neighbouring areas.
Use botanical extract sprays (such as neem seed extract, lemongrass or ginger) 1:15 litres of water.
Use 10 tablespoons of liquid soap per 10 litres of water.
Spray plants every week in the evening until whitefly population has been reduced.
Release parasitic wasps from the genus
Encarsia formosa if commercially available in your area.
